samples.question: This picture shows hoses pinned flat on a plain board. Exactly one hose is drawn in a strong colour; every other mark is plain grey, and every grey mark is decoration that must be ignored - no grey mark touches the coloured hose. The coloured hose is one connected hose that runs in straight horizontal and vertical stretches and changes direction only by right angles. One end of the coloured hose is capped by a solid coloured block, and that capped end is where the walk starts; the other end is a plain cut. Walk along the coloured hose from the capped end to the plain end, never leaving the hose and never skipping a stretch. At each right-angle change of direction you turn either to your left or to your right, judged from the direction you are travelling at that moment as the picture is seen. Count every such turn along the whole walk. A coiled hose in this picture need not keep curling the same way, and the turns near the capped end need not agree with the majority. Does the walk contain more left turns or more right turns? Answer with exactly one of: left, right.
